analysis:
The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date (head line 3), adds `python3 scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py` to the test command list (head line 998), and adds a paragraph (head lines 1023-1031) describing that script. The script runs the CI runner routing shell step against a loopback HTTPS plane with a throwaway certificate and covers the default-off switch, fork PRs, exact label grants, HTTP errors, retry, timeouts, untrusted or plain-HTTP planes and hostile reply text. It also pins each routed job's fallback, timeout and read-only permissions, and keeps release workflows on literal Blacksmith runners. The doc states that no check contacts the real plane.

No source, runtime, protocol, key handling, attestation, cache or authorization code is modified, so none of the provider-side threat entries is affected (T-041 prefix cache, TB-002, TB-003, TB-011, A-008 and the rest). The new text is a security-positive test description: fork PR handling, release workflows pinned to literal runners, and untrusted-plane rejection. It makes no claim that weakens a threat-model assumption or implies production qualification.

Open integration questions, all outside the supplied evidence: whether scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py exists, whether the build.md#ci-runner-routing anchor exists, and whether the workflow behaves as described. These are documentation-accuracy items, not demonstrated security regressions. I found no concrete finding.
